sources.title: Zero-shot learning - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Zero-shot learning (ZSL) is a problem setup in machine learning where, at test time, a learner observes samples from classes which were not observed during training, and needs to predict their class. The name is a play on words based on the earlier concept of one-shot learning in computer vision, in which classification can be learned from only one example. sources.title: Zero Shot transfer | AI Research Papers
sources.snippet: Zero-shot transfer, in the realm of AI/ML, describes the ability of a model to perform a task or classify data without having been explicitly trained on examples of that specific task or data. Instead, the model leverages prior knowledge gained from training on different, but related, tasks or data.

sources.title: Zero Shot transfer learning | AI Research Papers
sources.snippet: Zero-shot transfer learning empowers AI models to perform tasks they haven't explicitly been trained on. Unlike traditional machine learning, which requires labeled data for each task, zero-shot learning leverages prior knowledge from related tasks or semantic descriptions to generalize to unseen scenarios.
